name: The Crown Inn

layers.essential_history: [[c:The walk starts and finishes at the Crown Inn on Duck Street. The oldest part of the building dates from the early 1600s, when Elton was at its busiest, with around a thousand people: weavers, craftsmen, yeomen and farmers.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:The village has had many names: Adelintune in the Domesday Book of 1086, then Aethelington, Aylington, Aillington and Ailton, before settling on Elton.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Midnight, July 1587. The innkeeper's daughter runs to you at the door: the Queen's servants are frantic. The little silver casket they guarded all the way from Fotheringhay has gone. On the stable floor she found a scrap of paper, written in a simple code.]]

sources.title: Elton Parish Council: A short history of Elton

directions_to_next: [[c:From the Crown, walk down past the green to Stocks Green, about 140 metres.]]
support: [[c:Support the village: have a drink at the Crown before your walk, or book a table for when you get back.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The servant's scrap]]
puzzle.intro: [[c:Each letter has been moved one place along the alphabet. Move each one back a place (B becomes A, C becomes B).]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Where was the casket taken at midnight? (one word)]]
hints: [[c:Start with the first word: U, I, F.]]
[[c:U becomes T, I becomes H, F becomes E.]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:It says THE FORD AT MIDNIGHT. Someone carried the casket towards the river crossing.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? The answer is a place where people crossed the river before there was a bridge.]]

evidence: [[c:A coded note says the casket went to the ford at midnight.]]
